claim: Explicitly re-encoding cropped image regions through vision encoders ensures precise attention to regions of interest but increases computational cost, whereas a re-sampling strategy reduces computational overhead.
falsifier: One could compare the two strategies on a visual reasoning task, measuring both accuracy and inference time.

conditions: the model uses a vision encoder for tokenization
the regions are cropped from the original image
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system (Argus framework) and the specific re-encoding and re-sampling implementations; transfer beyond these is unestablished.

title: Choice of explicit engagement–precision of attention boundary
